function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been observed for millennia (e.g., static electricity from amber), but its systematic study began in the 17th–18th centuries. Key figures include William Gilbert (discovered magnetism and coined “electricus”), Benjamin Franklin (identified positive/negative charges and invented the lightning rod), Alessandro Volta (invented the voltaic pile, first battery), and later scientists like Michael Faraday (electromagnetism) and James Clerk Maxwell (unified electromagnetism). So while no single person “discovered” electricity, it was developed through contributions from many pioneers.
